decisions.executionNote: Approach the two nearer upright supports with each arm in its own workspace; gradually pitch grippers downward and preserve elbow-up continuity.
Visually align each wrist over its nearer support and descend slowly; exact fingertip offset remains uncertain.
Fine-align to visible block axes, compensating wrist rotation with lateral translation; approach grasp centers without closing yet.
Center the supports between the jaws, close fully, and lift 2 cm to check retention visually.
Both supports appear retained. Lift clear and carry to symmetric base locations, rotating their long axes into alignment while keeping grips closed.
Lower the two retained blocks to the table at equal spacing and release without lateral motion.
Withdraw from the released supports, then turn both open grippers inward above the lower board while staying on their respective sides.
Finish turning inward and align the open jaws above the lower board's two ends; supports remain upright and separated.
Descend to grasp both ends of the lower board with matched orientations, then close fully before lifting.
Lift the lower board level using both closed grippers, then begin translating toward the two upright base supports.
Center the held lower board over the two base supports and lower it evenly to their tops.
The board is still slightly above the supports. Seat it another two centimeters, open both grippers, and withdraw outward/upward to verify stability.
Lower board remains on the supports. Move outward clear of it and rotate toward the remaining white blocks, maintaining mirrored elbow-up paths.
Align above the remaining supports using wrist views, compensating tool reach and right-block yaw; descend only to a pregrasp height.
Advance along each wrist's viewing direction to the grasp plane, correct right-block lateral offset, and close both jaws.
Wrist views show the blocks too far down-frame for centered grasps. Reopen, shift jaws back over their centers, and close again without lifting yet.
Lift the newly centered grasps clear of the table, check visual retention, and begin carrying the blocks inward above the completed lower board.
Both blocks remain visible in the jaws. Carry them to symmetric middle-support locations above the board and finish aligning their axes.
Lower both middle supports vertically onto the centered lower board, then release without disturbing their spacing.
Clear the released middle supports upward and backward, then turn both open grippers inward toward the middle board.
The middle supports are upright on the lower board. Finish mirrored gripper alignment and approach the middle board's two ends from above.
Descend symmetrically to the middle board's grasp height, making a small orientation correction, then close both grippers.
Lift the middle board level with both grippers closed, providing clearance above the middle supports before translating it.
Carry the visibly retained middle board straight over its two supports, keeping both ends level and centered.
Seat the middle board level onto its two supports and open both grippers, allowing it to settle before withdrawing.
Withdraw from the released middle board, then move each arm toward the top piece on its own side without crossing over the tower.
Approach the small top board with the left arm, turning to grasp across its narrow dimension; hold the right arm clear.
Use the left wrist view to align with the small board's slight yaw and approach its grasp plane slowly.
Fine-center the small board between the left jaws, descend to its side edges, and close fully before testing retention.
Lift the small board clear of the table with the left gripper closed, then begin turning its long axis across the tower.
Carry the small board above the center of the completed middle layer, finishing its horizontal alignment while keeping it level and retained.
Fine-center the small top board, lower it onto the middle board, release, and lift away to inspect its placement.
The small board rests on the tower. Retract the left arm clear while moving the open right gripper toward the green top piece from its own side.
Pitch and lower the right gripper toward the green piece, using its wrist view for alignment; begin returning the empty left arm along a continuous elbow-up path.
Fine-align the right jaws with the green piece's yaw, lower to its sides and close; finish the empty left arm's return toward origin.
Lift the green top piece with the right gripper closed and align its axes while clearing the table; keep the empty left arm at origin.
The green piece remains retained. Carry it inward above the small top board, stopping with the right EE on its own side of the centerline.
Lower the green piece toward the top board and make a small centering correction; retain it until seating height is visually checked.
Seat the centered green top piece gently, open the right gripper, then begin withdrawing upward and outward without touching the tower.
The released green piece stays on the top board. Clear the tower upward and outward, then begin returning the open right arm toward origin.
All eight pieces appear upright and centered. Continue the open right arm's gradual return, maintaining clearance and elbow-up continuity.
